# ADR-0004: Approved AI vendors and third-party services

**Status:** accepted · **Date:** 2026-11-14 · generated by `new-project`; edit freely, it is yours now.

## Context

Which model vendors may see this project's code and data is a data-governance decision, so it is recorded before any agent runs.

## Decision

**Decision:** the vendors listed under Consequences may receive this project's code and data, and the third-party services below receive only what their row says.

### Third-party services the presets send data to

None beyond the cloud provider in ADR-0001.

### Third-party services this project sends data to

Added 2026-11-14 (issue #1). Each row says what leaves the repo or the running app.

| Service | Role | What it receives |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (approved vendor) | Specialist agents and the Verifier's notes, via `langchain-anthropic`; Claude Code builds W0, L1–L3, L6, W2 and W3 | Users' comparison inputs, search results, page text fetched during a run; repository code (Claude Code); through ElevenLabs, voice-agent transcripts and tool results (issue #37) |
| Keenable | Web search and page fetch, via `langchain-keenable` | Search queries built from the comparison inputs; URLs to fetch |
| Neon | Postgres for runs, sources, claims, events | Everything a run produces: the comparison inputs a person typed, and quotes from public pages that can name people. No accounts or contact details |
| Render | Hosts the container (ADR-0005) | The built image, its environment secrets, and everything the running app handles: comparison inputs, run data on its way to Neon, and request logs |
| Vercel | Hosts the landing page (lane L6, ADR-0005) | The landing page's own repository and build; no code from this repository and no run data |
| Mel (desktop agentic terminal) | Builds lane L5 (`ui/`) | Repository code; Mel runs on an OpenAI key (an approved vendor, set 2026-11-14). Switching Mel to another vendor needs that vendor added to the approved list first |
| OpenAI Codex CLI (approved vendor) | Builds lane L4 (`db/`, `api/`) | Repository code |
| OpenAI API (approved vendor) | Backup LLM for the voice agent, through ElevenLabs (issue #37) | When the primary and first backup models are unavailable: voice-agent transcripts and tool results |
| FAL | Generates the submission's OG image (the link-preview picture) via the Skillry `bs-duolingo-style-og` skill | One headline, the product name and a one-line context; no code or run data |
| Skillry | Distributes that skill | Nothing from this repo; installs files under `~/.claude/skills` |
| ElevenLabs | Narrates the demo video; runs the "Ask Receipts" voice agent (`agent_3401m7egdn2xexfte0d12vcewt09`) and publishes its widget, which is served from unpkg.com (added 2026-11-15, the owner's decision, issue #37) | The narration script text. From landing-page visitors, **only after they click "Talk to Receipts"** (the widget is click-to-load; a plain page view contacts only Vercel, the page's host): the widget's config request (IP address, user agent, referring page); a browser-fingerprint user id (FingerprintJS `visitorId`, stored in the visitor's `localStorage` as `elevenlabs_convai_user_id`); their voice and typed messages and the transcripts; and the run list and battlecards the agent's two read-only tools fetch from the app's public API, including quotes from public pages that can name people. Agent settings, set by the main session through the ElevenLabs API on 2026-11-15 and read back from its responses (not checkable from this repository): voice audio not recorded, transcripts kept 30 days, file uploads off, calls end at 300 s, at most 3 at once and 50 per day, and an origin allowlist of `receipts-landing-nine.vercel.app` with the origin header required. Browsers on other sites are refused; a script can forge the header, so the daily cap (50 calls of at most 300 s) is what bounds the cost. The agent's LLM (the language model that writes its replies) runs through ElevenLabs: Claude Haiku 5.5, with backups Claude Sonnet 5.5 then GPT-5.4-mini, so transcripts and tool results also reach Anthropic or OpenAI. ElevenLabs' default model (DeepSeek) was replaced because DeepSeek is not an approved vendor |
| unpkg.com (served via Cloudflare) | Serves the pinned widget script, `@elevenlabs/convai-widget-embed@0.22.2` (issue #37) | After a visitor clicks "Talk to Receipts": the visitor's IP address, user agent and referring page. The version is pinned; the file has no subresource-integrity hash, so its content is not pinned |
| Google (storage.googleapis.com) | The widget loads its avatar texture and language-flag images from `storage.googleapis.com/eleven-public-cdn` (issue #37). Its stylesheet also has an `@import` of Google Fonts, which browsers ignore because it follows another rule, so fonts.googleapis.com is not contacted (judge round 2 on #38) | After the click: the visitor's IP address, user agent and referring page |
| cdn.jsdelivr.net; m1.openfpcdn.io (FingerprintJS) | Conditional widget requests: an audio-resampling worklet when the browser can't set the sample rate; FingerprintJS's monitoring ping on about 1 in 1,000 fingerprint loads (issue #37) | Only in those cases, after the click: the visitor's IP address, user agent and referring page |

## Consequences

The orchestrator reads this file before routing a task to a model.

- anthropic — Claude family; default for planning, orchestration and implementation in this kit
- openai — GPT family and Codex CLI

## Alternatives considered

google, meta, mistral, zhipu, xai
